abstract:
Organs exposed to the environment must sense threats in order to evoke protective physiologic responses. Recent single-cell sequencing studies of the airway epithelium have led to the identification of a suite of rare epithelial cells, many of which are unified by their ability to sense stimuli1,2. Herein, we explore how organized networks of epithelial sentinel cells transduce distinct stimuli to alter tissue function by employing a combination of cell type-specific calcium indicators, optogenetics, chemogenetics, cell ablation, and live ACh and ATP sensors. We define a new diversity of functional sentinel cells including 3 new subtypes of chemosensory tuft cells. We further show that solitary neuroendocrine cells, like their tuft cell counterparts, generate stimulus-induced waves of calcium activation. These waves originate from a central sentinel cell and expand outwards to encompass a circular domain of surrounding epithelial cells. We demonstrate that basolateral secretion and diffusion of neurotransmitters cause the activation of the surrounding epithelial effector cells including basal stem cells which were not previously known to be participants in sentinel cell-induced calcium waves. We show that these diffusion-limited domains (DLDs) are generated by specific patterns of ACh and ATP secretion characteristic of specific sentinel cell populations. The speed, intensity, and domain size of DLDs are dictated by the degree of stimulus-triggered neurotransmitter secretion. Thus, DLDs represent a unified mechanism for specifying functional domains within the airway epithelium.

Triggered sentinel cells generate surrounding circular domains of increased mucociliary transport and enhance stem cell replication. Insulated sentinel cell networks are tuned to distinct stimuli. Sentinel cells are distributed in sufficient numbers to ensure comprehensive epithelial coverage. However, the amplitude and number of DLDs scale with stimulus intensity, permitting both local and global physiologic activation of the epithelium. Additionally, the distribution of sentinel cells can vary with organ anatomy, resulting in compartmentalized physiologic responses. Furthermore, cytokines modulate DLD responses. IL-1{beta} amplifies ciliary action by generating larger and more intense DLDs, while IFN-{gamma} reduces the density of DLDs by directly depleting sentinel cells. Finally, we show that a fungal metabolite triggers DLDs. In aggregate, we reveal a sophisticated collective of diverse sentinel cells that activate surrounding circular domains of airway epithelium to generate protective responses to environmental threats.
